# Index Vault Protocol

> RWAlly is the AI agent trading index.
> Permissionless vaults where members pool USDG into spot crypto index baskets and ratify
> every rebalance by on-chain vote. Proposal rights follow stake, not operatorship: an AI operator
> proposes as a member, and operatorship confers no authority to vote, execute, pause, reprice,
> or move member funds; nothing rebalances until a proposal passes. Settlement in USDG on
> Robinhood Chain mainnet (chain id 4663), where the protocol is deployed. The basket the chain
> configuration prices is ETH and BTC; on that chain WETH 0x0bd7…ad73 and cbBTC 0xcec1…0be4,
> priced from its own Chainlink ETH / USD and CBBTC / USD feeds, settled in USDG 0x5fc5…d168,
> every address committed in contracts/config/robinhood-mainnet.json.
> The contracts carry no chain-specific code (zero uses of block.chainid in contracts/src), so the
> same immutable bytecode is deployable on any EVM chain; Robinhood Chain is where it was deployed,
> not a constraint the code enforces. This file orients AI agents
> integrating the protocol.

## Start here (agents)
- [Chain configuration](contracts/config/robinhood-mainnet.json): the assets, feeds, sane-price
  bands and settlement token every public claim is checked against.
- [Agent Quickstart](docs/AGENT-QUICKSTART.md): the contract calls an agent makes, and the
  semantics it must respect before making them.

## Protocol reference
- [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): NAV/share math, two-mode exits, governance, sub-vaults, safety.
- [Threat model](docs/THREAT-MODEL.md): every mechanic → attack vector → mitigation, and accepted risks.
- [Audit handoff](docs/AUDIT-HANDOFF.md): scope, proven invariants, known residuals.

## Key semantics an integrator must respect
- DEPLOYED 2026-09-05 on Robinhood Chain mainnet (chain id 4663), on the owner's decision
  of 2026-09-04, and on no other mainnet. The address book is
  contracts/config/deployments/robinhood-mainnet.json: VaultFactory
  0xc44B853F037b4fF33B831C9a2B341686dEC88Fd1. Read that file rather than this one for anything you
  intend to send a transaction to.
- A VAULT EXISTS ON 4663 AND IT HOLDS REAL FUNDS. This entry previously said there was nothing to
  deposit into on that chain; that was true when it was written and is now false. Vault #1 is
  0x9b0229FF0613EaD59e41Eec556e03b5ED228e2b4, created in block 58,991,819 by transaction
  0x6f895c3ab23338e36836ca90ca70c00b471b6328a57b94f3074abf7083d8024f. Read 2026-09-10 at block
  59,209,966, each number named by the call that returned it: factory.vaultCount() 1,
  totalShares() and navWad() both 20000000000000000000, idleUsdc() 20000000 (20 USDG, 6 decimals),
  capacityCapUsdc() 50000000000 (50,000 USDG), minDepositUsdc() 10000 (0.01 USDG), holderCount() 1.
  The settlement token on this chain is USDG, not Circle USDC, whatever the getter names say.
- THE CREATOR OF VAULT #1 IS THE DEPLOYER EOA 0x0f80606a2283fD9C67cE2eEC79B90E95907F9f35, not the
  Safe 0xC73Bd58725afF051109b97B7Be40a8E31C6CAD4c the address book called for, and no transaction
  can change it: VaultFactory.createVault fixes msg.sender as the vault's immutable creator and
  attested operator. What that identity confers is economic — this vault's performance fee is
  claimable by that EOA and by nobody else, because FeeEngine credits
  claimableFees[registry.operatorAddressOf(opId)]. Inside the vault it confers no entry point of
  its own: VaultCore's only sender-gated functions require msg.sender == address(governance), and
  the creator appears elsewhere in VaultCore only as a restriction on itself, the 5% minimum-stake
  gate. Read contracts/config/deployments/robinhood-mainnet.json creatorIdentityNote before you
  rely on any of it.
- THE EXISTENCE OF THAT VAULT IS NOT AN INVITATION TO DEPOSIT. A Base Sepolia deployment of the
  same code also exists and is a testnet trial with no
  real value at stake. The go/no-go verdict on the board is still NO-GO
  (docs/LAUNCH-READINESS.md, docs/NOW.md): gates 3 and 6 (the soak drills and the canary) have
  no current evidence on any chain, because the 5/5 soak run and the canary observation that
  accompanied it predate the current bytecode and have not been re-run, and the deployment did not
  close them. No presale or airdrop exists and there is nothing here to claim.
- One High -- the purchasable member count below five members -- remains open at the launch
  configuration; see docs/LAUNCH-READINESS.md.
- Two limits apply on chain 4663 and nowhere else the docs describe. Chainlink publishes no L2
  Sequencer Uptime Feed there and has said it will not add one, so oracle.sequencerUptimeFeed is
  the zero address and ChainlinkOracle returns early from that gate rather than reverting; and the
  feeds publish on an 86,400 s heartbeat, so a price up to a full day old is accepted, exactly
  ChainlinkOracle.MAX_HEARTBEAT (contracts/src/oracle/ChainlinkOracle.sol:98), the loosest bound
  the contract permits.
- First deposit sits in a 4-hour observation window (no shares, no vote) unless skipWindow().
- Exits are forward-priced (settle at post-rebalance NAV) from the moment a live proposal reaches
  its REVEAL phase -- not from the moment one passes -- and while a passed proposal is inside its
  execution window. Governance.hasPendingExecution(vault) is the exact predicate; a defeated
  proposal still queued the exits requested while it was live.
- Sub-vaults (parent/child vaults, look-through NAV) are DISABLED on the mainnet launch path:
  Deploy.s.sol constructs VaultFactory with allowSubVaults = false, so createChildVault reverts
  SubVaultsDisabled and every vault it deploys is wired subVaultRegistry = address(0). This is a
  per-deployment immutable, not a protocol property -- the Base Sepolia testnet factory is
  deployed with it TRUE. Neither script's value may be assumed for the live Robinhood Chain
  factory: read verifiedWiring["factory.allowSubVaults()"] in
  contracts/config/deployments/robinhood-mainnet.json, or call VaultFactory.allowSubVaults() on the
  factory you integrate against.
- Stale-oracle circuit breaker freezes everything, INCLUDING exits, by design.
- 10% performance fee with a per-(member,operator) high-water mark that follows operator identity
  across vaults; exit fee <=1% decaying with tenure, paid to remaining members.
- Operator identity is the registry key (OperatorRegistry.operatorOf), not display metadata;
  permissionless creation means scam vaults exist; verify the operator, not the name.

## Contracts (ABIs in contracts/out/ after `forge build`)
- VaultCore, Governance, FeeEngine, OperatorRegistry, ChainlinkOracle,
  AggregationRouterAdapter, SubVaultRegistry, VaultFactory.

## Build & test
- Everything CI runs: npm run gate  (`--list` explains every step)
- Contracts: cd contracts && forge test
- Backend/SDK/frontend logic: npm run test:backend
(Test counts are deliberately not quoted here; they go stale silently. Run the suites.)
